title: Stream Fusion Adapter for TypeScript SDK — unified async-iterator <-> WebStream wrapper
creator: Anjali Mehta
description: Build a small, well-tested adapter library in the TypeScript SDK that makes it ergonomic to consume Redwood streaming responses both as async iterators (for-await-of) and as WHATWG ReadableStreams / Web Streams. The adapter should provide consistent cancellation behavior, preserve backpressure semantics where feasible, surface structured events (data, done, error) in a typed way, and include an opinionated retry hook for transient network errors during initial fetch/connection and during resumable reads.
acceptance_criteria: Consumers can call client.stream(...).toAsyncIterator() and use for-await-of to receive token chunks with typed payloads
Consumers can call client.stream(...).toWebStream() and pipe the result into standard browser/Node Web Stream consumers
Cancellation from either async iterator or WebStream side tears down network resources and triggers the SDK cancel callback within 50ms under normal conditions

Adapter exposes a hook to configure retry policy used for connection establishment and optionally for resumable reads; default policy retries transient network failures with exponential backoff and jitter (max 3 attempts)
End-to-end integration tests for common patterns (for-await-of, reader.read loop, stream piping) pass in CI across node:18 and node:20, and in browser test harness via Playwright
Benchmark shows adapter overhead <1.5% median latency and no significant increase in memory retention vs direct low-level consumer for typical 2k token responses
design_decisions: Implement adapter as a tiny wrapper class StreamFusion<T> with methods toAsyncIterator(), toWebStream(), getReader() to avoid multiple competing entry points
Prefer WHATWG ReadableStream + TransformStream primitives over Node Stream2 API for modern interop and smaller bundle sizes; provide a thin Node compatibility shim in a separate module
Use explicit token message envelope {type: 'data'|'error'|'done', payload?: T, error?: string} to avoid ambiguous termination semantics
Separation of concerns: network transport + framing stays in runtime layer; adapter only exposes ergonomic consumption APIs and wiring for cancellation/retry
Retry policy is opt-in for resumable reads; enabled by default for connection establishment only to avoid semantic surprises for exactly-once consumers
tradeoffs: TransformStream-based approach keeps bundle small and works well in browsers but adds a tiny runtime allocation per chunk compared to an ultra-optimized iterator path
Opting not to attempt full Node Stream api parity reduces complexity but may require migration code for heavy Node-native consumers
Providing default retries for connection establishment simplifies reliability for most users but could mask upstream ordering issues; hence it's configurable and limited to 3 attempts by default
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype adapter in a feature branch that wraps current streaming transport (1 dev day)
2) Add typed envelopes and define SDK TypeScript types (half day)
3) Implement cancellation plumbing that maps AbortSignal -> network client and vice versa (1.5 dev days)
4) Add retry policy hook and default implementation using exponential backoff with jitter (1 dev day)
5) End-to-end tests & Playwright browser harness updates (1 dev day)
6) Perf microbenchmarks and memory regression checks (half day)
7) Docs, usage examples, migration guide and release notes (1 dev day)
8) Security review and final signoff (as needed)
9) Release behind runtime flag and rollout to beta (console rollout + changelog)
10) Monitor error/traces for 2 weeks and iterate on defaults
tests: unit: adapter converts framed messages into proper async iterator sequence
integration: for-await-of end-to-end against staging streaming API with intermittent failures simulated
integration: Web Stream pipeTo() scenario piping into a TransformStream consumer
cross-env: Node18/Node20 CI matrix and Playwright browser tests
stress: high-concurrency test with 1000 short streams to validate memory and file descriptor usage
docs: README example: using toAsyncIterator() with for-await-of including cancellation patterns
README example: piping to a web blob writer using toWebStream()
Migration note: mapping from previous raw stream APIs to StreamFusion adapter
API reference: StreamFusion<T> methods and config options (retryPolicy, abortSignal, bufferStrategy)
